description: The problem involves a system where outputs feed back into inputs, creating reinforcing or balancing dynamics that a linear analysis would miss. The structural question is whether the proposed intervention accounts for how the system will respond.
detect_when: Actions create reactions that amplify or dampen the original effect — reinforcing or balancing loops
There are delays between action and visible consequence that distort feedback
The system has self-correcting or self-reinforcing behavior that the answer treats as static
The answer recommends an intervention without considering how the system will adapt or respond
coverage_signals: The answer identifies feedback loops — reinforcing (virtuous/vicious cycles) or balancing (homeostatic)
The answer accounts for delays between cause and effect — not just immediate consequences
The answer considers second and third-order consequences of the proposed action
The answer identifies leverage points where small interventions produce large systemic effects
materiality_test: Would accounting for feedback dynamics change the recommended intervention or its expected outcome?
reasoning_demanded: systems analysis, loop identification, delay recognition, leverage point detection
curation_note: Systems-thinking provides the foundational framework for seeing interconnections rather than linear cause-effect chains. Feedback-loops identifies the specific loop structures (reinforcing and balancing). Second-order-thinking extends analysis beyond immediate consequences. Non-linear-dynamics addresses disproportionate cause-effect relationships. Leverage-points identifies where small interventions produce outsized systemic effects. Delays addresses the temporal gap between action and consequence that distorts feedback. Note: systems-thinking also appears in causal-diagnosis — there it traces causal chains; here it identifies systemic feedback structures.

detect_when.note: Detection conditions from feedback-loops (reinforcing/balancing dynamics), delays (temporal gap distortion), second-order-thinking (beyond immediate consequences), leverage-points (small input, large effect).

coverage_signals.note: Loop identification from feedback-loops. Delay accounting from delays. Higher-order consequences from second-order-thinking. Leverage points from leverage-points.

models.note: Six models — comprehensive coverage of the system dynamics territory. Systems-thinking cross-listed with causal-diagnosis: acceptable because structural purposes differ (causal tracing vs feedback structure identification).
